message: Function "<anonymous>" uses a user-supplied ID without verifying ownership in the same function scope.
fix: After extracting the ID, verify ownership within the same function: "if (resource.userId !== session.user.id) return 403".

attackPath: Attacker requests GET /users/victim-id which reaches the handler mounted at /users.
Handler returns 401 when req.user is missing and 403 when req.params.id does not match req.user.id.
Only matching-id requests reach the parameterized SELECT query.
reasoning.impact: No data is exposed; mismatched IDs are blocked with 403 before the database query, so another user's record cannot be read.

evidence.quote: const rows = await db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?', [req.params.id]);

reasoning.fixSummary: No further change needed; keep the 401 check and the String(req.params.id) !== String(req.user.id) ownership check before the query.
reasoning.plainLanguage: Someone who is logged in can now only see their own profile, and any request for someone else's details is blocked. Your users' private information stays private, so there is no extra risk from this page.

message: Function "<anonymous>" uses a user-supplied ID without verifying ownership in the same function scope.
fix: After extracting the ID, verify ownership within the same function: "if (resource.userId !== session.user.id) return 403".

preconditions: Request must have an authenticated user (req.user), otherwise it is rejected with 401.
attackPath: Authenticated attacker sends DELETE /users/:id with another user's id.
Server compares the requested id to the caller's own id and admin role and rejects non-owners with 403.
Delete query runs only after that ownership check passes.
reasoning.impact: No unauthorized deletion occurs; non-owners are blocked with 403 and unauthenticated callers with 401.

evidence.quote: await db.query('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?', [req.params.id]);

reasoning.fixSummary: No change needed; retain the existing owner-or-admin check before the delete.
reasoning.plainLanguage: An outsider cannot delete another person's account because the system checks ownership before deleting. This means your customers are protected from having their accounts removed by someone else.

message: State-changing route with no CSRF protection
fix: Add CSRF protection to state-changing endpoints. Options: (1) Use SameSite=Lax or Strict cookies. (2) Implement double-submit cookie pattern. (3) Check Origin/Referer headers. (4) Use a CSRF token library like csrf-csrf. Without CSRF protection, attackers can trigger actions on behalf of your users from external sites.

message: No error monitoring/alerting dependency found (Sentry, Rollbar, Bugsnag, Datadog…). Production errors will fail silently — you won't know the app is broken until a user tells you.
fix: Add an error monitor: @sentry/nextjs (or @sentry/node), Rollbar, or Bugsnag — wire it to capture unhandled errors and alert you. If your host already provides this, treat this as informational.
